data.description: Common grammar patterns for Turkish learners
learningPoints: Focuses on grammar patterns commonly influenced by Turkish sentence structure.
Improves control of prepositions and auxiliary verbs.
Builds accuracy with articles, verb forms, and natural phrasing.
Strengthens sentence structure for international communication.
Helps avoid frequent mistakes in professional and academic English.
ESOL B1–B2 and aligns with IELTS 5.5–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 60–94 score ranges.

sections.explain: In English we say 'married to someone', not 'married with someone'.
English requires an article before singular countable nouns.

words.word: I bought a new car yesterday.
I bought the new car yesterday one.

sections.explain: The verb 'discuss' does not require the word 'about'.

words.word: We discussed about the problem yesterday.
We discussed on the problem yesterday.

sections.summary: Use present simple for general habits.
sections.explain: Present continuous should not be used for general habits.

words.word: She is drinking coffee every morning.

sections.summary: Use correct verb forms after 'want to'.
sections.explain: After 'to', the base form of the verb is required.
In English we say 'turn on' or 'turn off' the light.

words.word: Many people work in this company.
Many person work in this company.
Many peoples work in this company.

sections.explain: Past actions require past tense verbs.

words.word: She went to the meeting yesterday.
She go to the meeting yesterday.
She gone to the meeting yesterday.
